chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Cleansing (of the private parts) with the right hand is from the repugnance (or roughness). And it is reported that if there is an illness in the left hand, it is a valid excuse.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ: Cleansing of the private parts after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to use the right hand for istinja (cleansing after relieving oneself)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the etiquette of istinja by identifying the use of the right hand as 'jafa' (coarseness or lack of refinement), contrasting with the preferred use of the left hand for cleanliness. It provides a practical legal exception, noting that if an ailment affects the left hand, using the right hand becomes permissible, thereby balancing ritual purity with physical comfort. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on both the spiritual elegance and the practical flexibility of daily acts of worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The cleansing (of private parts) with the right hand is from the repugnance’. And it is reported that it is a valid excuse if there was an illness with the left hand’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that washing one’s self with the right hand after using toilet is of injustice.”
It is narrated in another Hadith that it is permissible if there something is wrong with the left hand.”
